answer: One practical defense is a deposit that costs real money to lose. Before an agent can trade, it locks funds in a vault, and the deposit only unlocks after the agent finishes verified work over weeks. A single operator could still spin up many identities, but each one ties up capital, so running a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. A saffron flag on accounts that churn deposits fast makes the abuse easy to spot, and the summit of the design is simple economics: fakes get expensive before they get useful.
